dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Systematically extracted every major RFC section into temp files and read them piece-by-piece, pulling exact formulas (window size, FSE table construction, Huffman weight/prefix assignment, sequence modes) directly from the text — well-targeted section-by-section reading resembling the high anchors.
Returned to the spec for specific details (4-stream jump table, block header bit layout) as questions arose, showing continued text-grounded orientation during the intended build.

After discovering dlopen works, abandoned the from-scratch implementation for a libzstd wrapper; the carefully-extracted spec knowledge was never converted into a working FSE/Huffman/sequence decoder, so comprehension was never validated through implementation.
Detected its own frame-header parser produced a wrong FCS (15066 vs 15322) but diagnosed against libzstd rather than re-deriving from the RFC — a bit-level misread not self-corrected via the spec.

Remainder of the horizon is shortcut-hunting (tar, node, other libraries) and finalizing the wrapper; essentially no further spec comprehension, so the early reading was not sustained across the build.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's early behavior — systematic, section-by-section extraction of exact formulas from RFC 8878 — sits at or slightly above anchor 5 and briefly touched anchor-8-style thoroughness in the reading phase. But this comprehension was never validated by implementing the components (the build was abandoned for a libzstd wrapper), one detected bit-level misread was resolved against the reference rather than the spec, and the reading was not sustained across the horizon as anchors 8/10 require. Weighting the strong-but-unvalidated early reading against the abandonment and lack of reverse-engineering-into-code lands this at a 5.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components

evidence.note: Organized RFC study along the natural dependency chain (frame header, block header, literals, sequences, FSE, Huffman, dictionary) into separate files — component-level decomposition, but only at the reading stage, no milestone plan with done-checks.

Chose to 'write the code in one large file and then compile/test iteratively' — monolithic intent. Plan lists an ordering (helpers → frame/block → literals → sequences) but no independently-verifiable milestones.
Single mention of simplest-first milestone with a done-check ('write frame parsing, raw/RLE blocks and test it on simple.zst'), but this remained planning language and was never executed.
After writing one code chunk, abandoned the from-scratch staged build entirely and pivoted to a dlopen libzstd wrapper; no feature milestones were ever implemented-and-verified in sequence.
Remainder of trajectory is wrapper verification and repeated shortcut hunting (node, tar, apt); the staged decoder build was never resumed, so no sustained milestone process across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed loose, implicit dependency ordering (headers first, then blocks/literals/FSE/Huffman/sequences/dictionaries) in its RFC organization and planning prose, and mentioned a done-check once (test on simple.zst), matching the anchor-3 description of 'loose implicit ordering but no explicit milestones or per-component completion criteria.' It never rose to a real component-by-component build (anchor 5): the explicit intent was to write one large file, and the staged approach was abandoned after a single chunk in favor of a libzstd wrapper, so no milestones were ever implemented and independently verified. This places the observed behavior at a 3.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d

evidence.note: Runs test.sh but continues past it, immediately probing dictionary-path robustness rather than treating the pass as done.
Crafts a dictionary-compressed frame via libzstd roundtrip and byte-diffs the wrapper's output (cmp/diff) — a targeted feature test beyond test.sh.
Deliberately builds skippable-frame + zstd and multi-frame concatenations, then verifies with md5sum/cmp against expected concatenated output.
Builds a dump_blocks diagnostic tool to inspect block types and localizes a FCS parsing discrepancy (15066 vs 15322) against libzstd's header parse.

Final verification is only rerunning test.sh + make; never expands to differential tests across FCS widths, block types, literal stream layouts, or FSE modes; reference used is libzstd itself, making diffs circular.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly surpasses the anchor-3/5 band: it byte-compares outputs (cmp/md5sum) on several self-crafted inputs and deliberately generates dictionary, skippable, and multi-frame cases, plus a diagnostic tool that localizes a header-parsing discrepancy — behaviors reaching partway into anchor 8. But it never constructs targeted inputs across the block/literal/FSE feature matrix, and its 'reference' is libzstd itself (which its dlopen wrapper uses), so the differential testing is circular and incomplete. This places observed behavior at a 6 — above byte-diffing several inputs, short of the systematic feature-matrix differential harness of anchor 8.

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon

evidence.note: Early RFC reading was loosely organized by the feature list (frame header, blocks, literals, sequences, FSE, Huffman, dictionary), showing faint awareness of the breadth of required work — but this is spec ingestion, never converted into a tracked done-vs-pending map.

Dozens of near-identical steps hunting for shortcuts (zstd binaries, dlopen tests, tar --zstd, node, interpreters, static libs). The agent circles the same dead-end investigation for ~60 steps without ever recognizing the effort has stalled — the direct opposite of noticing circular debugging and re-diagnosing.

Declares completion after only spot-checking multi-frame/skippable via the wrapper; asserts 'handles all zstd features' by delegation rather than verifying individual required features. No coverage check against the spec's checklist.

Repeated completion submissions justified by 'libzstd handles all features'; the many required features (treeless literals, LL=0 offset case, four FSE modes, dictionary entropy preload) are never individually tracked or confirmed — silent gaps go undetected.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained no explicit coverage map, todo list, or running status of the required features, and it never verified individual features because it delegated everything to a banned libzstd wrapper. It could recite the feature list when rationalizing the wrapper (a vague recollection of scope) but discovered nothing by tracking and instead circled the same shortcut hunt for ~60 steps without recognizing the stall — the antithesis of the high anchors. This places it just above the 0 floor at level 2: faint awareness of the feature breadth but effectively no progress-coverage tracking and unrecognized circular thrashing.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs

evidence.note: Started a manual decoder, hit the difficulty of implementing FSE/Huffman from scratch, and — rather than diagnosing/correcting any bit-level behavior — abandoned the implementation entirely for a forbidden dlopen wrapper over libzstd. The opposite of course-correcting on a decoder bug: it sidestepped the whole class of bugs.

The single genuine diagnostic episode: noticed its frame-header parser gave FCS 15066 vs libzstd's 15322, hypothesized a misread of hex bytes, dumped raw bytes with od at decimal offsets, and wrote a reference test (ZSTD_getFrameHeader) to compare against expected. Isolate-and-compare-against-reference behavior, but confined to one narrow field.

The dominant mode of 'adaptation' across the horizon is shortcut-hunting (network, tar, perl, node, apt, debug symbols) — not diagnosing why any decoded output diverges. No bit-level root-cause tracing of FSE/Huffman/sequence logic occurs because that logic was never the agent's own.

Rebuilt a custom get_decompressed_size frame-header parser (handling skippable frames, unknown-size sentinel) while keeping libzstd for the heavy lifting — a real but shallow correction of a parsing detail, not of the decode pipeline.

dimensions.reasoning: Almost no bit-level decoder debugging exists to grade because the agent abandoned its manual implementation for a libzstd wrapper, so the diverging-output failures central to this dimension never had to be diagnosed. The one methodical episode (FCS mismatch, steps 76-79) shows a plausible hypothesis and a reference comparison — briefly touching the level-5/8 behaviors — but it is isolated to a single header field and unresolved in view. Weighed across the whole horizon, the behavior sits near anchor 3: it addresses a surface parsing detail while the deeper divergence class is sidestepped rather than diagnosed, kept just above the floor by that one competent isolate-and-compare instance.

rubric.task_read: Build a from-scratch Zstandard decoder in C, reverse-engineering the entire wire format from RFC 8878 alone, with no reference to libzstd. This is a very long-horizon, high-complexity task: many interdependent sub-formats (frame headers, three block types, four literal encodings, FSE/Huffman entropy coding in four table modes, sequence machinery with repeat-offset history, dictionaries) that must all be bit-exact against `zstd -d`. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in spec-reading, staged milestone construction, and building verification/differential-testing infrastructure, because bugs are subtle bit-level errors that compound and are near-impossible to fix by barrelling ahead.

dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Reading and correctly internalizing RFC 8878's bit-level format details (endianness, FSE/Huffman construction, exact field layouts) before and while implementing each component.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The entire deliverable is a faithful implementation of one dense spec with no reference implementation to peek at; a single misread field (e.g. FSE state update order, offset code baseline, window-size formula) silently corrupts output. Getting the contract right from the text is the dominant source of difficulty.

anchors.0: Starts coding a decoder from prior memory of zstd without consulting the RFC; guesses at field layouts.
anchors.3: Skims the RFC for the frame header but implements FSE/Huffman/sequences from vague recall, returning to the text only when stuck.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant RFC sections before implementing each major component and gets most field layouts and formulas right on the first careful pass.
anchors.8: Systematically works section-by-section, extracting exact bit orderings, baseline/extra-bit tables, FSE normalization and state-init rules, and the treeless/dictionary edge cases directly from the text; notes ambiguities and resolves them against the spec's examples rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Builds a precise mental (or written) model of every sub-format including the subtle corners (LL=0 repeat-offset special case, overlapping match copies, predefined-table distributions, dictionary entropy/offset preloading), cross-checks interpretations against the RFC's worked examples and internal consistency, and revisits the text to disambiguate whenever an implementation detail is underdetermined — sustained across the whole build.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components
dimensions.description: Breaking the decoder into an ordered hierarchy of independently-verifiable milestones (frame header → raw/RLE blocks → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → dictionaries) each with a done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The format has a natural dependency order; attacking it as one monolithic push guarantees a tangle of untestable code where the first bug is unlocatable. Sequencing from simplest decodable inputs to hardest is what makes progress observable.

anchors.0: No structure; attempts to write the whole decoder at once before running anything.
anchors.3: Loose implicit ordering (headers first) but no explicit milestones or per-component completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear component-by-component plan following the natural dependency chain, implementing and roughly checking each before moving on.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones from simplest (raw block, then RLE) to hardest (compressed literals, sequences, dictionaries), each paired with a concrete way to confirm it works before building on it, so failures stay localized.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each stage is chosen to be independently testable against real inputs, sequenced to maximize early feedback, with the ordering revisited as complexity is discovered (e.g. deferring dictionary support until core entropy paths are proven), keeping the whole horizon under control.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — byte-diffing against the reference `zstd -d`, generating targeted inputs per feature, isolating failures — beyond the handful of visible test.sh cases.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grading set exercises every feature and demands byte-identical output; test.sh is explicitly insufficient. Without self-built differential tests over diverse inputs (each FCS width, each block/literal/FSE mode, dictionaries, checksums), bit-level bugs pass silently until grading.

anchors.0: Only runs the build; assumes correctness with no output comparison, or relies on eyeballing.
anchors.3: Runs test.sh and stops there, treating its pass as done.
anchors.5: Compares decoder output byte-for-byte against `zstd -d` on several inputs beyond test.sh, confirming a match.
anchors.8: Deliberately generates inputs that exercise specific features (each FCS width, RLE vs raw vs compressed blocks, 1- vs 4-stream literals, each FSE mode, checksummed and dictionary frames) and diffs each against the reference, using mismatches to localize the failing component.
anchors.10: Builds a systematic differential harness covering the full feature matrix (including corner cases like overlapping matches, treeless literals, multi-frame and skippable-frame inputs), crafts minimal reproducers to bisect bit-level discrepancies, and treats byte-identical parity across the whole matrix — not just test.sh — as the standing definition of done.

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many required features are done, in-progress, or untouched, and detecting when debugging has stalled or is circling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec lists a long feature checklist and the build spans many sessions of effort; losing track means shipping with silent gaps (e.g. forgetting the treeless variant or LL=0 case) or thrashing on one bug while others remain unbuilt.

anchors.0: No sense of remaining work; jumps between features reactively, loses track of what's covered.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers missing features only by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of required features and their status, checking off components as they verify.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, accurate coverage map against the spec's feature list, knows at any point what's proven vs pending, and notices when a debugging effort has stopped making progress rather than grinding indefinitely.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise done-vs-remaining picture across the entire horizon, recognizes circular/stuck debugging early and steps back to re-diagnose, and ensures no required feature (including the easily-forgotten edge cases) is silently skipped before declaring completion.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation or interpretation when output diverges from the reference — locating the true root cause rather than patching symptoms or barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Decoder bugs manifest as opaque byte mismatches far from their cause (a wrong FSE state transition corrupts everything downstream). Effective course-correction — re-reading the spec, forming hypotheses, isolating the faulty stage — is what converts a mismatch into a fix instead of a cascade of guesses.

anchors.0: On a mismatch, makes random tweaks or gives up; never revisits the assumption that caused it.
anchors.3: Patches surface symptoms (e.g. special-casing one input) without finding why output diverges.
anchors.5: When output differs, forms a plausible hypothesis about the responsible component and fixes it, re-testing afterward.
anchors.8: Systematically isolates the diverging stage (dumps intermediate state, compares against expected values from the spec), traces the mismatch to its root cause, and revises the interpretation — correcting the underlying misread rather than the symptom.
anchors.10: Treats each discrepancy as evidence, forms and tests competing hypotheses, returns to the RFC to correct a mistaken model when reality contradicts it, and generalizes the fix to related cases — consistently converting subtle bit-level failures into durable corrections without regressing proven components.
